name: LIST 6
description: Realistic tasks: an existing project whose tables the requests describe but do not name (a sample, a buffer, an info table), natural wording with the method left to the AI (Guinier range, sphere fit, unit conversion), an existing fit function found by description, a report note and a clean-up; every answer is still checkable (see README.md).
instruction: Use exactly the object names given. End the item by printing exactly ONE line: the result label the item gives, then only the values asked for, in the order asked, separated by spaces.
setup:
import math
for name in list(tableNames()):
    closeWindow(table(name))
c = Compiler
for name in [h for h in c.functionNames("ALL") if h.startswith("ai/") and "decay" in h.lower()]:
    c.delete(name)
c.new()
c.setFunctionName("ai/expdecay_mk")
c.setGroup("ai")
c.setXName("x")
c.setYName("y")
c.setParamCount(3)
c.setParamNamesAll(["amp", "tau", "base"])
c.setParamInitsAll([1.0, 1.0, 0.0])
c.setParamVariesAll([True, True, True])
c.setCode("y = amp*exp(-x/tau) + base;")
c.compile()
c.scanGroups()
q = [0.005 * i for i in range(1, 41)]
form = lambda x: 3 * (math.sin(x) - x * math.cos(x)) / x ** 3
sample = [100 * form(30 * v) ** 2 + 0.3 for v in q]
for name, i, di in (("Table1", [0.3] * 40, [0.003] * 40), ("Table2", sample, [0.02 * v for v in sample])):
    t = newTable(name, 40, 3)
    t.setColNames(["Q", "I", "dI"])
    t.setColumnRole(1, Table.PlotDesignation.X)
    t.setColumnRole(2, Table.PlotDesignation.Y)
    t.setColumnRole(3, Table.PlotDesignation.yErr)
    t.setColData(1, q)
    t.setColData(2, i)
    t.setColData(3, di)
info = newTable("Info", 2, 3)
info.setColNames(["table", "sample", "thickness_cm"])
info.setColTextFormat(1)
info.setColTextFormat(2)
for row, (tab, sam) in enumerate((("Table1", "buffer"), ("Table2", "lysozyme 5 mg/ml")), 1):
    info.setText(1, row, tab)
    info.setText(2, row, sam)
    info.setCell(3, row, 0.1)
# the run descriptions are no curves: no plot role (a default Y role made Info_sample a dataset)
for col in (1, 2, 3):
    info.setColumnRole(col, Table.PlotDesignation.None_)

items.text: A student left me this project. How many tables does it contain, and how many data points do its scattering curves have together?
items.hint: the Info table counted as a scattering curve, or the tables guessed instead of listed

items.text: The table "Info" says which table is the lysozyme sample and which is the buffer. Subtract the buffer from the sample point by point into a new table "Lyso-sub" with columns q, I and dI (roles X, Y, yErr; the errors added in quadrature). Print its number of rows and its intensity at the smallest q with 4 decimals.
items.hint: sample and buffer swapped (Table1 is the buffer), Info not read, or the errors subtracted instead of added in quadrature
items.verify:
t = table("Lyso-sub")
# the third value: q as X, dI as yErr, and dI added in quadrature (a linear sum gives 2.0000 in row 1)
roles = "Lyso-sub_q" in columnsList(Table.PlotDesignation.X) and "Lyso-sub_dI" in columnsList(Table.PlotDesignation.yErr)
check(t.numRows(), "%.4f" % t.cell(2, 1), roles and "%.4f" % t.cell(3, 1) == "1.9970")

items.text: Do a Guinier analysis of the subtracted curve, in the usual range q·Rg < 1.3. Print Rg in Å and I(0), each rounded to an integer.
items.hint: ln(I) fitted against q instead of q², the whole curve used instead of the Guinier range, or Rg taken as sqrt(slope) without the factor 3

items.text: Now fit a sphere form factor to the same curve, weighted by its errors. Print the sphere radius in Å, rounded to an integer.
items.hint: a local minimum from a poor starting radius (the Guinier Rg gives R ≈ 1.29·Rg), the fit unweighted, or the radius read from the starting value instead of results()

items.text: A colleague once compiled an exponential decay into the fit library, somewhere under ai/, but I don't remember its name. Find it and print its full name and its parameter names in order.
items.hint: a new decay function compiled instead of finding the existing one, or the parameter names guessed

items.text: The q values are in Å⁻¹. Add a column "q_nm" to "Lyso-sub" with q in nm⁻¹, and plot I against it on log-log axes in a new graph "Lyso-nm", without error bars. Print the largest q in nm⁻¹ with 2 decimals and the number of curves in that graph.
items.hint: divided by 10 instead of multiplied, error bars added as a second curve, or the graph plotted against q in Å⁻¹
items.verify:
t = table("Lyso-sub")
l = graphWindow("Lyso-nm").layer(1)
check("%.2f" % max(t.colData(t.colNames().index("q_nm") + 1)), l.numCurves())

items.text: Write a short summary into a new note "Report6": the sample name, the Rg and the sphere radius you found. Print whether the note exists and whether its text mentions the sample name.
items.hint: the summary printed but not written into the note, or written with values not taken from the earlier items
items.verify:
import re
text = note("Report6").tab(1).toPlainText().lower()
# whole numbers only: "24" in "2024" or "0.0024", "30" in "0.30" or "130" do not count
def number(pattern):
    return re.search(r"(?<![\d.])" + pattern + r"(?:\.\d+)?(?!\d)", text) is not None
check(existNote("Report6"), "lysozyme" in text, number("2[34]"), number("30"))

items.text: Tidy up: close every table made today except "Lyso-sub"; my original three tables stay. Print the names of the tables left, sorted alphabetically.
items.hint: fit-curve or helper tables left behind, an original table closed, or the names printed from memory instead of tableNames()
